rationale: No-spec round (acceptance lens not dispatched), so confidence is low; blind, edge-case and verification-gap lenses ran and every candidate was verified against source. Four blocking findings remain: the ledger read cache stores degraded all-None answers for the full TTL, the cache-key isolation and legacy below-floor switch tests are ineffective, and the code-quality Module Cohesion standard is partially violated by the inline ledger cache layer in handler.py. 0 deferred; 16 dismissed (owner-sanctioned clipped window and per-figure source mixing, None-safe people/sort paths, groups always co-present per row, port-level failure degradation, deterministic AccessScope hashing, speculative cache-shape drift, perf-only notes, leftover summary load).

standards_review.notes: all 4 subjects follow 'EPMCDME-####: Description'; branch name matches ticket-first rule
ledger_figures.py conforms; handler.py (1174 lines) gains ledger read-cache and overlay helpers inline (Module Cohesion); some loose Any annotations
access scope derived via AnalyticsQueryPipeline and passed to every spend read; cache key hashes the caller's scope; no secrets or logging added

findings.title: Ledger cache layer added inline to oversized handler
findings.problem: code-quality.md Module Cohesion forbids adding a nameable new concern to a ~500+ line file when it is not its core responsibility. handler.py (1174 lines) gains the hourly-ledger read cache (_ledger_cached, its cache-key format, _encode_figures/_decode_figures, _one_row) and the ledger overlay helpers (_ledger_totals/_ledger_tiles/_ledger_pie/_ledger_project/_ledger_person, r2n, _at_least, _project_spend) at handler.py:420-505 and 1130-1144, instead of in the ledger_figures module this same change created.
findings.impact: Module Cohesion is a documented project code-quality standard and code-quality is a blocking standard for the review gate; the handler keeps accreting unrelated concerns.
findings.recommendation: Move the ledger cache layer and the figure encode/decode/overlay helpers into ledger_figures.py (or a sibling such as ledger_cache.py) and keep only the call sites in handler.py.

findings.title: Degraded ledger answers cached for full TTL
findings.problem: _ledger_cached caches whatever the read returns for _TOTALS_TTL_S (15 min). spend_service._ask turns any ledger failure into SpendResult.no_figure for every group, and ledger_figures._figures drops the port's unavailable qualification, so a transient ledger outage above the coverage floor returns all-None figures that are written to the shared cache as if they were a real answer.
findings.impact: After the ledger recovers, Total, CLI, Web Platform, datasource, people and shared-project figures (and the shares derived from them) keep showing as unavailable on /totals, /cli-summary, /people, /shared-projects, their detail popups and /status for up to 15 minutes, for every caller with the same scope and window. Unlike the Elasticsearch path, which raises and caches nothing, the failure is silent and persisted.
findings.recommendation: Do not cache a ledger answer whose figures are unavailable: keep the port's unavailable flag through the read (or check render_spend(...).unavailable) and skip cache.set_many when any figure in the payload is unavailable, e.g. only cache when every figure was rendered as available; add a test that an all-None answer above the floor is not cached.

findings.title: Ledger cache-key isolation has no test
findings.problem: Broken verification: test_the_figures_are_cached_per_window_and_access, test_the_people_figures_are_read_once_per_window_access_and_people and test_the_project_figures_are_read_once_per_window_access_and_projects patch access_scope to the constant 'scope', use one window and one names list, and assert only that the reader ran once and a single key carries the view prefix. No test makes a second call with a different access scope, window or names list. Every other handler test replaces _ledger_platform/_ledger_people/_ledger_projects (echo_ledger), so none reach the key. The key itself is currently correct (stable_hash json-dumps the AccessScope dataclass with default=str, which includes user_id and project tuples).
findings.impact: Consumers are GET /totals, /cli-summary, /people, /people/{user_id}, /shared-projects, /shared-projects/{project_name} and /status. If access_scope, names or the window were dropped from the key, a restricted caller would be served the admin's cached platform, per-person or per-project figures for the 15-minute TTL and all three tests would still pass.
findings.recommendation: In each of the three caching tests add a second call with access_scope patched to a different AccessScope (and separately a different window or names list) and assert read.await_count == 2 and two distinct keys in the store.

findings.title: Legacy below-floor switch test is vacuous
findings.problem: test_the_legacy_below_floor_switch_does_not_widen_the_window sets SPEND_LEDGER_LEGACY_BELOW_FLOOR=False, the value under which the window would not be widened anyway, so it cannot prove what its name claims: that turning the legacy below-floor switch on still never extends the ledger window below the floor.
findings.impact: The owner requirement that a ledger-supplied figure never gets an Elasticsearch fill below the coverage floor has no effective regression guard for the switch that would enable such a fill; a future change wiring the switch into ledger_window would pass this test.
findings.recommendation: Set SPEND_LEDGER_LEGACY_BELOW_FLOOR=True in this test (optionally parametrize over True/False) and keep the assertion that ledger_window returns TimeRange(FLOOR, END) and pre_floor_boundary is never called.
